memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After the death of Moses the servant of the Lord, the Lord said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' aide: "Moses my servant is dead. Now then, you and all these people, get ready to cross the Jordan River into the land I am about to give to them — to the Israelites." — Josh 1:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses had led Israel for forty years. He was the man who spoke with God face to face, who stretched out his hand over the Red Sea, who carried the people's burdens on his shoulders. And now he was gone. You can imagine the fear that must have gripped the camp. Who could ever replace Moses?

But notice how God begins. He does not spend time in the past. He simply says, "Moses my servant is dead. Now then... get ready." God's work does not stop when a great leader passes away. God buries His workers, but His work goes on.

Maybe you have lost someone you leaned on — a parent, a mentor, a pastor, a friend. That loss is real, and God does not rush you past your grief. Yet He gently reminds you that He is still moving forward, and He is calling you to move with Him. The land was still promised. The plan was still on.

The same God who was with Moses is the God who comes to us in Christ, who says, "I am with you always, to the very end of the age" (Matt 28:20). Leaders change; our unchanging Lord does not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you stuck looking back at a loss instead of stepping into what God has next?
2. What is the "Jordan" God may be asking you to cross right now?
3. Do you trust that God's plan does not depend on any one person?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when the people I lean on are taken from me, help me remember that You remain. Give me courage to step forward into what You have prepared. Amen.
